fatal_errors: The proposed plasma-nitriding treatment does not reconstruct the target atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating followed by 550 °C annealing.
The proposed chloride/acid immersion conditions omit the target 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical testing and 900 °C cyclic molten-salt hot-corrosion tests.
The claimed 20–30% reduction in mass loss is unsupported by cited evidence or supplied data.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the correct broad problem and plasma nitriding can plausibly improve stainless-steel corrosion resistance through expanded-austenite formation when processing avoids chromium-nitride precipitation. It also provides an appropriate untreated control and a reasonably falsifiable electrochemical comparison. However, it is a different surface-engineering route from the target HEA coating, with different microstructure, mechanism, exposure conditions, and performance metrics. Agreement is limited to the generic prediction of improved passivity and corrosion resistance. The 400–500 °C window is also overly broad because the upper end can promote nitride precipitation and chromium depletion, potentially worsening corrosion. With no cited evidence, the quantitative benefit remains speculative.
